itemized.summary: A code comment claimed a staleness tripwire validated each exemption's stated fact, when the check is only structural.
A compound shell command could hide a second invocation from the census check.
The census header pattern also matched the Retired table.
A Retired heading was counted as an examined census table.
A new growth test case depended on the real index staying under 50 rows, so it would break as the index grew.
The test-side number speller stopped at 99.
The heading capture read one token, so it could not parse a count like One hundred.
The comment post did not pass an explicit repository, so it could land on the current directory's repository.
The issue listing used to find the store was not properly bounded.
The repository map was not keyed by OWNER/NAME, allowing a lookup to resolve the wrong repository.
Test stubs ignored the query they were given, so tests could pass regardless of what was asked.
Host matching did not require exactly github.com.
The HTTP readiness probe lacked a deadline and could hang on an open SSE stream.
The probe did not handle the negotiated MCP protocol version.
Readiness could report ready without every scope being ok.
Dangling symlinks were read as installed components.
An npx-based probe could install or pass from a warm cache rather than measuring actual readiness.
Package-manager exec command forms were not recognised by the readiness parser.
MCP response envelopes were not validated before being accepted.
HTTP protocol errors were reported by type only, losing the actual cause.
A documented backup recipe was wrong, found in two places.
A documented remedy using a project flag did not work as stated.
An unreadable Makefile was silently treated as empty.
A rule declaring multiple targets was refused membership.
A non-string kind value crashed the parser.
The Makefile parser backtracked a ::= assignment into a rule.
A registered control's invocation was not bound to its target, so it could run something else and pass.
A repository without a scripts directory skipped Makefile examination entirely.
A define block body was parsed as rules.
A same-session reconcile deleted its own uncommitted approved section while keeping the run id, so the guard then blocked it.
The legacy snapshot prefix was dropped on a second approval.
A head check with no run file present accepted a marked record.
A marker line inside an issue body could forge a run boundary.
A malformed run file reopened the legacy fallback path.
A second run was blamed for files committed by an earlier run.
The run-start marker blamed a run for upstream changes merged later, and a rebase silently widened its scope.
Two high-severity findings: the scope report did not redact sensitive values.
Structured endpoint definitions were not compared correctly.
An unset environment variable in a definition was mishandled.
A malformed local-scope config was not reported as such.
The OK verdict was not given per name, misreporting mixed results.
Same-owner detection compared pids but ignored the host, so a local caller sharing a remote holder's pid skipped the refusal.
Streamed jq parsing let trailing garbage after a JSON object pass as a partial read.
A jq alternative operator read an entry whose value is false as absent.
A command-line flag was accepted but silently ignored.
A printed revert instruction was unsafe and could discard work.
A bare wait-for-CI flag swallowed the following PR number argument.
An empty observed CI status rollup was reported as green.
The retry's containment check ran before its sleep and re-poll rather than after.
The CI wait recipe could finish on the wrong event.
The strict-event option was missing on the GitHub Actions lane, which had no tests.
The observed verdict came from a second, unclassified snapshot instead of the one classified.
The branch-delete target was not tied to the repository that had been checked.
A failed worktree scan still allowed branch deletion.
Re-verification reused a stale default branch and stale worktree list.
The committer-date fallback did not enforce the 24-hour age rule.
The destination remote check ignored the host.
The verified remote URL was discarded before the push, so the push could go elsewhere.
An unreadable PR listing was treated as the branch having no PR.
A guard did not validate the Codex entry, so it passed under mutation.
A guard matched the remedy text anywhere in the document, so it passed under mutation.
The skip test could pass even if every gate had been skipped.
The regression test relied on a fixed half-second delay instead of an event.
The regression test used the parent pid, which reparenting could change.
The regression test lacked a skip guard for hosts without procfs.
Two child fixtures shared the same ready-file path, so one could see the other's readiness signal.
A pull_request trigger with a target-branch filter satisfied the CI trigger classifier.
An extra push entry with an empty branch list returned no violations.
A config parse-error source excerpt could print a secret.
Falsey or wrong-type config shapes silently defaulted or crashed.
Non-UTF-8 config input escaped the refusal path.
YAML parser and regex error messages could still echo a secret value.
Mixed-type keys crashed a sort call.
A generated YAML hint broke on an apostrophe.
A swallowed directory listing error resolved as a complete enumeration.
Any stack at the repository root was counted as covering components.
The summary kept only one stack per directory.
Exclusion test fixtures sat too deep in the tree to ever fail.
A resolved verdict did not disclose that enumeration was depth-bounded.
A symlinked directory let a neighbouring checkout change the enumeration result.
The already-merged path could delete a branch that had been pushed to or recreated since the merge.
A branch at the same commit was treated as the PR's branch and could be deleted.
Generated skill mirrors were stale relative to their sources.
A failed worktree listing was reported as zero worktrees.
Fork PRs and unreadable fork metadata were run through a divergence check that does not apply.
CI lane classification accepted status contexts other than the intended CI system's.
A documented snippet ignored enumeration and per-worktree failures and broke on paths with spaces.
A mode name claimed a single run when it only measured a single summary region.
Documentation claimed an expired CI wait meant the pipeline never registered.
A shell -c script starting with an environment assignment was dropped entirely as an assignment.
A shell invocation with options before -c was not recognised as running a script.
A mid-word hash character was treated as a comment and cut the command.
A backslash-newline continuation split the shell from its -c argument.
A gitignore pattern swallowed the control's fixture files, so the control did not exist in a clean clone.
An undecidable result was scored as a GOOD control outcome.
A stub exception could be reported as unreachable rather than a refusal.
Exit 0 was scored as success without requiring a serving verdict.
A missing or unreadable turn record was accepted as reviewer evidence.
Abbreviated and full commit hashes were compared as plain strings.
The worktree delivery verdict did not examine ignored files, which could hold undelivered work.
Files marked assume-unchanged could hide modifications from the delivery verdict.
A missing helper caused the PR-head stop check to be skipped rather than stopping.
A reconcile step could leave divergent scratch files staged, and its result was not checked.
A generated Codex mirror was stale relative to its source.
A missing gh binary crashed the head check instead of reporting unverified.
A starvation test became vacuous once release cleared the PR field, so it could no longer fail.
Rewriting output to use echo lost reader names that look like echo options.
An unquoted revision list was subject to pathname expansion.
A lint suppression reason was false because the function it justified had no caller.
A line-bounded read dropped entries after a newline and bypassed all-or-nothing validation.
A new test asserted against the real checkout's git filter config, so it could fail spuriously on hosts with extra filters.
A fresh test repository still inherited the system gitconfig, which the sanitised environment did not exclude.
An orphaned consuming watcher could steal another session's mail.
awk compared role identifiers 1 and 01 as equal numbers.
An option value placed after a flag could disguise a consuming orphan as a peeking reader.
A zombie owner process never triggered the owner-gone state.
Three new tests lacked a skip guard for a missing jq binary.
The control runner scored a crashing checker as unavailable instead of unsignalled.
A detection step keyed on a retired hook's name, so it could not see the file actually shipped.
A retracted claim survived in the body of a file whose title had been corrected.
The scan counted paths rather than reads, so hundreds of unopened files reported zero offenders.
An untracked local note or a user's own opted-in settings file was reported as a project regression.
A same-line JSON grep let a formatter-wrapped registration pass untouched.
A fixed-size text window missed a four-line claim and fused two unrelated bullets.
The regression test drove its own copy of the walker, so stubbing the production scanner left it green.
An unreadable new surface was absorbed by an aggregate threshold and never visited by the narrow scan.
A standalone at-rest use of a file was flagged as a hook registration.
An ignored leftover file was reported as a regression, contradicting the change's own migration path.
Parsing both fields through one integer conversion turned a prefixed issue number into a slug, silently dropping its hold.
A control adapter matched an error message also printed for missing or malformed files, so a broken fixture would score as a miss.
A re-gate condition missed the moved resync path, so a resync-only change could reach squash unvalidated and unpushed.
The tripwire's block tracking mishandled elif and trailing comments, reading a correctly placed call as gated.
A multiline if or tilde-fenced block hid a real gated call, returning an empty list as if all were examined.
The generator's own output file was accepted as input and returned a confident mirror list.
A hyphen collision gave a nonexistent source a neighbouring skill's mirrors.
Equivalent path spellings produced different answers.
The output was a concatenation rather than a deduplicated set.
A non-mutation test compared exit codes, which cannot distinguish an unchanged tree from a rewrite.
A manifest-exclusion test used real outputs where every case had a manifest, so it could not detect an unconditional rule.
A diagnostic sat only inside the success branch, so failing runs got no explanation.
A test assertion was satisfied by echoed payload on stdout, so it could not fail.
New shell tests lacked guards for missing git and bash binaries.
A match window crossing a newline let a following paragraph trigger a false refusal of a legitimate merge directive.
A negated sentence with a possessive reference fired both guards, requiring two overrides.
A denylist environment sanitiser let a git tracing variable escape.
Generated mirrors kept the old case-fold code because the resync ran before the correction.
A worked example named the wrong implementation.
Shell behaviour claims were stated universally though they vary by shell and version.
A repair paragraph contradicted itself about whether quoting helps.
A duration claim was unsupported by dates; the conflict had stood for days, not months.
An index row described a match verdict the hook does not expose.
Malformed JSON input fell through to allow in an approval-gate hook.
An absent python3 fell through to allow in an approval-gate hook.
A broken git directory setting fell through to allow in an approval-gate hook.
Repository discovery used the hook's working directory rather than the edit's target.
Suffix path matching exempted lookalike paths nested elsewhere.
Refusals were written to stdout although the blocking reason is read from stderr.
Committed evidence claimed a case would flip under conditions its fixed-payload runner cannot produce.
A real-repo guard matched the enclosing repository's state, so it still reported fail with its planted defect removed.
A crash test passed when the gate never started because an unusable temp directory satisfied its assertions.
Six new tests lacked guards for a missing git binary.
A capped issue listing truncated silently, so a larger population read as fully covered.
An empty live file from a failed fetch was reported ok on both axes.
A ledger row recording nothing discharged a new obligation.
A malformed file crashed with the exit code reserved for a ledger defect.
A fixed capture date was printed for every snapshot, including freshly refreshed ones.
A string-valued mandatory flag read as false, so a violated criterion left the population and the record reported clean.
An unhashable status value crashed with the failure exit code and no verdict, and the caller swallowed it.
An artifact of a different kind was read as a verified result.
A reachability test passed when the gate never executed and matched a neighbour's path filter.
State was lost across separate shell invocations, which tests concealed by running both blocks in one shell.
A commit message overclaimed that the test cases could not pass while the documented commands were wrong.
The measurement mounted a fresh temp directory, destroying part of what it measured and manufacturing an empty result.
Unchecked setup let a failed stage run and be mislabelled.
An IPC health check matched echoed text and had its exit status inverted.
A provenance detector hardcoded three paths instead of deriving the checkouts.
A recall claim was not supported by the committed evidence.
A review receipt whose status said nothing passed as a completed review.
83 tests were left unguarded against a missing git binary.
A history scan counted skipped reviews as reviews.
Per-issue review coverage was read as per-change coverage.
A Codex-only install could not resolve the helper.
Control fixture verdicts depended on the host's default branch name setting.
A skip reason starting with a dash was read by grep as an option and passed the allowlist.
Mixed issue statuses erased a recorded skip.
The history scan accepted skips that had no committed reason.
One test remained unguarded against a missing git binary.
An isolation probe inserted the install directory into the import path itself, supplying the answer it checked.
A manifest labelled working-tree bytes with the HEAD commit hash, attributing uncommitted changes to a commit.
Known-bad checks discarded exit status, accepting a comparator that printed drift and exited 0.
A workflow validator checked field presence rather than values.
A PATH assertion checked host inventory rather than the isolated environment.
A blind anchor's stated claim was false.
An empty-manifest test used a disjunction that let it pass trivially.
A shared Makefile reader adapter lost every phony declaration, flipping phony status for all targets.
An import of a namespace package could resolve a foreign package of the same name elsewhere on the path.
A pinned target count could not discriminate a parser regression from a legitimate new target.
A failed replayed step was not reopened on the next resume, so a red tree was accepted as success.
The control kept its verdicts even with its subject disabled, so it measured something else.
A settled record carried a stale failure reason from the previous run.
Empty flag values read as omitted and silently resolved a different scope, examining the host registry instead.
An all-flags empty-value test passed because its cases named a harness binary that does not exist.
A diagnostic filtered on a hardcoded marker allowlist that dropped some drift markers.
A tripwire could not tell a re-sync condition from a neighbour's unrelated path match.
A call-site test counted filename mentions, so deleting an invocation still passed.
A non-zero check was treated as repairable drift, reporting resynced having fixed nothing.
A bare helper call exited 127 in repositories without the helper instead of being a no-op.
A control fixture kept a marker in the shared temp directory that concurrent worktrees would race on.
An availability check counted every entry in a shared commands directory, so an unrelated file announced the install present.
Link and change counts recorded intentions rather than results, reporting installed after a failed link.
Orphan pruning bypassed the new guard.
The good control case's link did not resolve.
Locator tests depended on ambient host state.
An overlap check covered only the case loop, letting an anchor supply ambiguous evidence.
An UNKNOWN observation was counted as proof the gate's tool was present.
The overlap check fired on runs already observed unavailable, turning an environment fact into a manifest accusation.
The clean-run check had the same anchor-side gap as the overlap check.
A substring match on a serialized verdict map let an undeclared verdict resolve to the success exit code.
A check read the refusal marker from one shell only, so a crash in the other counted as an identical refusal.
Sharing the host pid namespace could defeat the namespace signal used to derive host vantage.
A roster dropped declaration provenance.
A control invocation inherited a caller's environment variable, so its verdict reflected the caller.
A rejected declaration could inject a forged vantage line into the consumer.
The same forged-line injection was possible on the source line.
The help option printed nothing and exited 0.
An absolute gate path could escape the sandbox.
Battery runs had side effects across a shared sandbox.
A zero-count declaration certified an accepted coverage gap.
Containment was checked only on the baseline run.
Sandboxes were rebuilt from a moving checkout.
A gate that detected its bad input but claimed a missing tool on the good input was excused as unavailable.
Two controls on one gate were counted as two instruments, inflating coverage.
A mere mention of a staged-binary path was credited as staging.
A neighbouring command's PATH prefix was credited to the battery step.
The register globbed files rather than sharing the battery's discovery function.
An inert shebang was required as a dependency.
A new denominator counted exemptions as guards.
Commands that only echoed or printed a staging path still credited staging.
A command-local PATH override was credited as battery staging.
A similarly named backup directory matched as the staging directory.
An echo of the battery's path selected the wrong CI step.
Two existing tests still called a removed function.
A registered-case guard keyed on the repository's live ledger, so a neighbour's record could mask a fixture that stopped discriminating.
The live-fixture eligibility guard had the same dependence on the repository's ledger.
Nine import contexts that execute at import time were classified as deferred and reported clean.
A first-party source rule leaked globally and via absolute paths, so checkout location changed the verdict.
Virtualenvs entered the scanned population because pruning was by name only.
A selftest read exit codes, so an unrelated failure could stand in for the planted detection.
Nested source modules were flattened to the wrong import name.
Subtree scoping still exempted files with no import-path setup.
The hardened selftest accepted two unrelated lines each supplying half the expected signal.
Cache validation did not validate exclusivity.
An eagerly evaluated default let a hijacked default abort runs that supplied an explicit override.
An enumeration comparing keys missed a duplicated call.
A known-command-set test pinned only three of fourteen commands.
Token-membership matching let a daemon for one role match another role's pidfile.
A marker token was also a legal wave name, so matching could hit the wrong daemon.
A test overwrote the pidfile, so the reaper could not rediscover the leaked daemon.
A guard read a scanner report field as evidence of a CLI skip, backed by a fixture built to belief rather than tool output.
Scanner recursion disagreed with the pruned population, so a dependency inside a virtualenv reddened the gate.
A directory walk swallowed an unreadable subtree and reported a smaller population as clean.
A relative tool path broke when run from a child working directory.
An exact-token argv screen let equivalent skip-option spellings through.
A build-file guard could not tell the scanner's skip option from a neighbour's similarly named option.
A stated blind spot of the count check was overclaimed.
An early exit keyed on a managed count of zero hid an entirely unmarked package population.
An unmeasured count was folded in with zero, turning an unknown population into an asserted absence.
Substring matching falsely established reachability, producing a false pass.
A name rule was ASCII-only while claiming to enforce a specification that allows unicode.
An unreadable candidate was dropped, making the remaining attributions look unanimous.
Branch-suffix matching could attribute a neighbouring repository's rollout.
A non-string timestamp field aborted the scan of every other receipt.
An empty case registration passed the self-test.
A generated copy was synced before the fixes and carried the old code.
Line splitting also broke on unicode line separators legal inside JSON strings, refusing valid records and reporting an older model.
A CI guard matched a test-runner name as a substring of a helper script name, so a command running no tests satisfied it.
The guard accepted a resolver being invoked even when its result was discarded.
A prohibition on automatic worker count missed a quoted spelling.
The same prohibition falsely rejected an unrelated grep command.
Zero-padded worker count values were mishandled by the resolver.
A secret file was protected by umask only, which does not change the mode of an existing world-readable file on rerun.
A crontab pipeline wiped the operator's existing crontab entries.
A greedy parser took the last issue number in a branch name, letting a guard approve deleting the wrong worktree.
A pid-only self-identity shortcut bypassed the ownership witness and disabled an independent occupancy check.
A stale-takeover message asserted the owner was gone for all three possible causes.
A repository name containing an issue token put a foreign issue number ahead of the branch's.
A successful takeover inherited the previous claim's stale reason, misattributing the old owner's expiry.
A colour-forcing git setting hid every diff hunk, so real deletions counted as zero.
Deleted and added lines resembling diff headers ended the hunk early.
A documented reset recipe pinned an already-moved base.
A failed diff generation was reported as clean.
A readability test passed for directories and read failures were discarded.
A cleanup block ran before the traceback, so tailing output deleted the marker line.
One recognised header let an otherwise unparsed input pass.
A pipeline returned the sort's status, so a partial find population read as whole.
Binary patch sections were mis-parsed, counting two deleted binaries as one file.
Hunk counters could underflow without reporting malformed input.
A flush failure bypassed the marker and exited with an unrelated status.
The enforcement test searched the whole file, so it would pass a marker moved to the wrong channel.
A declined tool-call status was not counted as a tool error.
Generated bundles shipped a resolver without the guard beside it, so a bundled run installed nothing.
Uninstall on a repository with no hook yet recorded nothing, so an early opt-out silently failed.
A failed git config write was announced as a recorded opt-out.
The hook never consulted the opt-out setting, so a shared hooks path let another repository re-arm it.
Fence closure compared only the delimiter character, not its length.
An indented delimiter closed a fence early, restoring a phantom verdict.
Cited continuation fields reached a live gate.
A quote token inside a fence vanished from the citation count, making a zero ambiguous.
An empty blockquote marker counted as a live pushback argument.
An index-based stash drop was racy against other stash writers.
The installer ignored a configured hooks path and installed to the default location.
The check reported a non-executable hook as current.
A documentation pin did not require the conditional form of stash pop.
A substring tag match could select a longer sibling tag.
The restore pin accepted a bare stash apply.
Command splitting was quote-unaware in both directions.
Stem matching let one file inherit another file's exclusion accounting.
A row inside a multi-line HTML comment still counted as a live census row.
The coverage denominator counted fenced and commented example rows.
Resume dropped carried coverage from the roll-up, restoring a false green.
An unknown coverage state was omitted rather than recorded, and a test pinned the omission.
Unreadable files were counted as examined, so a scan that opened nothing reported coverage.
One component's count was read as the whole stage's coverage.
A mixed aggregate attributed another tool's examined files to the named component.
A global dedupe collapsed distinct invocations within a stream.
Consumer instructions still carried a stage-wide coverage overclaim.
Resume dropped a partially empty coverage carry.
A malformed time-to-live setting made a shelf-life guard fail open.
The planner reported nothing wrong about a population it had not inspected.
A lookup referenced an unset variable, matched hundreds of rollouts and returned an unrelated session's model.
A dependency carrying a skip reason was counted as audited.
The export omitted dependency groups and platform markers, leaving locked requirements silently outside the verdict.
A ledger test forbade the residual from ever reaching zero.
Coverage keyed on package name alone dropped an unaudited conditional version.
A selftest read findings without checking anything was examined, so an empty report passed.
A suppression for a package never audited on this platform was labelled stale.
A security assessment bounded local attackers by counting login-shell accounts, which does not bound who can plant a symlink.
An attack scenario described an attacker-owned target that the upstream check actually rejects.
Prefix matching on version ranges condemned a host that a disjunctive range admits.
A major-only version comparison missed a minor-version requirement.
A backward version move was reported as upgraded.
A tripwire scored an empty population clean and pooled verdict variables across lanes.
Shell version parsing mis-read short ranges and prerelease suffixes, reporting a release as a downgrade.
A doc guard searched the whole section, so a neighbouring signal's caveat satisfied it.
Paragraph anchoring let a caution naming two signals satisfy the guard for only one.
A typo in a narrowing flag returned clear over an empty population.
A roster entry with a missing or unrecognised liveness value cleared the retirement.
A valid JSON prefix followed by garbage was accepted as a partial result.
A control resolved the installed helper and read a host file, so its blindness depended on ambient state.
Two emitted JSON arrays passed a line-count guard and the gate printed clear with a live role present.
Generated mirrors were stale and would have failed CI.
A reversal trigger could not attribute an unknown result to this branch.
The reverse check read headings only, so a stale bullet for a deleted script scored clean.
Forward and reverse checks parsed headings differently, so an incidental mention stood in for a missing entry.
Fenced examples were read as document content.
A four-backtick fence was closed by an inner three-backtick fence.
A declaration inside a fenced example widened the allowlist and suppressed a real stale entry.
HTML comments were stripped before fences, deleting every entry between a fenced marker and a later comment.
Revendoring wrote all files before validating the fetched snapshot, leaving the tree replaced under an old manifest.
Revendoring required a valid manifest, refusing the input it exists to repair.
The offline gate gained a dependency on a URL field its comparison never reads.
An in-sync tree still exited with failure over a deleted pin file.
A doc pointed readers to the wrong numbered item of a step for the review stage.
Substring marker matching let a welded or swapped region still compare equal.
Two new Make targets were not declared phony.
